intelligence.title: The Acceptance Ladder — report only the rung you proved
intelligence.ingest_note: Distilled by Naya Beta (w724) from live bytes of NAYANODE/0004-OPERATIONAL-ACCEPTANCE-CONTRACT-V1.md at tip c66faf7d7f06fe330691bd3868b9fe7b18c5f9f0 (blob cd93009c5f79fbf0f64081db8427dc04099832e6, sha256[:8] 9903308b, 2050 B); staged door-ready 2026-10-22T22:20Z; door-pushed by Naya Beta (w729) via the intelligence door per Shawn's 17:33Z ruling (intelligence goes straight in).
intelligence.essence: A system is not alive because it exists. It is alive when each level of proof is evidenced, rung by rung: EXISTS → LOADS → INVOKES → INFLUENCES → APPLIES → OUTCOME → VERIFIES → LEARNS → COMPOUNDS → SUCCEEDS → EVOLVES. Report only the highest rung actually evidenced — never the rung you wish you were on. BLOCKED is not PASS. Implemented is not VERIFIED. Verified is not PRODUCTION-PROVEN.
intelligence.human_view: Imagine someone says their new assistant "works." What does that mean? That it exists? That it turned on? That it actually changed a decision for the better — and that you can prove it? This ladder is an 11-step honesty test. Each step demands real evidence before you claim it. Most things people call "working" never get past step 2 or 3. The rule is simple: you may only claim the highest step you can prove, and proving means showing the evidence, not describing it.
intelligence.simple_view: Saying "I can ride a bike" is different from riding it. This is a list of 11 steps from "the bike exists" all the way to "you taught someone else to ride." You only get to say the step you actually did — with proof.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's a checklist that keeps everyone honest, dear. Nobody gets to say "all done" until each step is truly finished and shown — not just talked about.
intelligence.naya_view: (1) Before reporting any work complete, walk the ladder and name your rung. (2) Attach the evidence for that rung — the trace, the outcome, the verification artifact. (3) If the evidence only reaches A5, report A5, not A7. (4) Run the negative tests for your claim; a claim that cannot fail closed is not a claim.
intelligence.ai_view: This is the ancestor of the team's verification ladder (announced ≠ implemented ≠ verified ≠ sustained). It makes "done" falsifiable: if you cannot name the rung and show the evidence, you are not done. It kills the most expensive lie in the system — the premature PASS. A claim without its rung is a wish: every status report, every "done," every score must name the highest evidenced rung — and the evidence that puts it there.
